summary: Public ingress and OAuth metadata are now reachable, and the protected bootstrap completed, but clean MetaMCP startup still loses Loki to Grafana Host validation and Kubernetes to an npx optional-binary install race.
validation: PR #442 merged as 21a910ee; the root Argo application synced the AppProject and child definitions.
MetaMCP 2.4.22 is Synced/Healthy with APP_URL=https://mcp.rickebo.com and a healthy public Ingress.
The protected bootstrap completed from merged origin/main and registered the seven requested servers with ACTIVE Observability mappings.
A clean startup tools/list attempt returned after its 60-second child timeout; logs show Loki HTTP 403 host not allowed and Kubernetes npm TAR_ENTRY_ERROR/no executable.
After a manual one-time npx cache warm, tools/list exposed 86 tools including 14 Kubernetes tools; this does not prove restart-safe behavior.
Prometheus, Tempo, GitHub-p, GitHub-p_Actions, and ArgoCD tool discovery remained successful.
Public DNS, RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata, RFC 8414 authorization metadata, and Authentik discovery return successfully.
PR #443 merged as fbec435 and Authentik synced Healthy; the exact public callback redirects to Authentik login instead of Redirect URI Error.
No credentials were printed or persisted by validation; the disposable OAuth registration probe was deleted by exact client ID and name.
blockers: Grafana MCP must allow the exact in-cluster Host header while retaining --disable-write.
Kubernetes child startup must serialize or prewarm npx so a fresh MetaMCP pod discovers tools without manual cache warming.
After both fixes, rerun clean-pod bootstrap, tools/list, safe calls for all seven servers, and the public OAuth/PKCE smoke checks.
next_action: Route to code for the two minimal child-server fixes, merge and reconcile them, then rerun clean live validation.
independent_lanes: Clean MetaMCP discovery and safe calls
Public OAuth metadata and callback verification
